panels.shot: Wide, high angle. A narrow old-town street in heavy rain. The hero walks under a streetlamp with Nero at his heel. A small shop sign glows amber: Bell & Sons, Horloger.

lines.text: Three nights since Club Noir. The rain had not stopped. Neither had the clocks.

panels.shot: Interior, warm amber light. Clocks on every wall. Augustin Bell puts a bowl of soup on the bench. The hero sits, still in his wet coat.

lines.speaker: Bell
lines.text: Eat, Elias. You look like a man who broke something expensive.

panels.shot: Close-up on Bell's face, half in shadow, pipe smoke curling. His eyes are serious.

lines.speaker: Bell
lines.text: Malaspina was a tenor. There is a whole choir. And every choir needs someone to keep time.

panels.shot: Night. Exterior, low angle. A black car idles outside, wipers moving. A gloved hand strikes a silver tuning fork against the shop door frame.

lines.text: In this city, a tuning fork is a death notice.

panels.shot: The shop explodes outward. Glass and clock faces fly into the rain. In the foreground, Nero drags the hero out of the doorway by his collar.

lines.text: The dog pulled me out. Nobody pulled Bell out.
